headline: Curated structure and binding datasets benchmark predictors and ligand recognition
label: Curated Biomolecular Structure Resources
summary: Structure predictors and ML models increasingly depend on curated, experimentally anchored datasets for binder discrimination and ligand recognition.
synthesis: The common thread is curated, experimentally anchored data resources used to evaluate and train structure-based predictors. POISK provides 89,074 patent-derived antibody-antigen records to test six structure predictors on binder versus decoy discrimination. SMARTFlexDB pairs 1187 apo-holo RNA pocket structures with conformational-change descriptors, and ARIEL links 278 nonredundant RNA-ligand complexes to experimental Kd values spanning nine orders of magnitude. PED 2027 extends ensemble coverage to integrate experimental and predicted IDP/IDR conformations, while SAbDab2 adds versioned train/test splits for machine-learning use. A physics-based pose prediction study reports 74% success on SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV main proteases and examines the role of receptor flexibility. DeepPhage and DBAASP V4 extend this resource logic to peptide discovery. What is new is the emphasis on benchmark-ready splits and condition-resolved or flexibility-aware annotations rather than sequence-only inference.
